steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write a short introduction for our paper on personalized Hindi speech recognition and translation for videos: why building a dataset is the hard part for a low-resource language, how we create a custom dataset from a small amount of one person's audio, fine-tune XLSR Wav2Vec2 on it, and wrap transcription plus English translation in a web GUI that outputs subtitled video.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Why training ASR is hard, especially for low-resource and personalized Hindi
2. Our method: RVC model -> custom Hindi Common Voice corpus -> fine-tuned XLSR Wav2Vec2
3. Web GUI pipeline: Hindi video in, English-subtitled video out
4. Contribution

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Problem
- ASR training formidable; model quality tied to dataset quality
- low-resource language like Hindi: far less online data than English
- personalized Hindi ASR: transcribe + translate an individual's unique voice
- generating a suitable dataset = significant hurdle

2. Method
- just 14 minutes of personalized custom audio -> train Retrieval-Based Voice Conversion (RVC) model
- RVC model -> tailored Common Voice 16 corpus for Hindi
- Cross-lingual Self-supervised Representations (XLSR) Wav2Vec2 trained on this dataset; adaptable with limited resources

3. GUI
- user-friendly web-based Graphical User Interface (GUI), built with Gradio
- Hindi audio -> Hindi text (XLSR Wav2Vec2) -> English text (mBART)
- input: video with Hindi audio; output: video with accurate English subtitles

4. Contribution
- advances ASR for low-resource languages
- streamlined pipeline: personalized transcription + translation, Hindi audio -> English subtitles, for video content

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Training an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model is a hard task, and how well the model works depends a lot on the quality of the dataset that is used in training. The challenge is even bigger when we try to train an ASR model for a low-resource language like Hindi, where there is much less data available online than for languages like English. It gets more complex again when the goal is to train a personalized ASR model for Hindi, one that does not just transcribe but also translates the unique voice of an individual. Generating a suitable dataset is a big hurdle for reaching this goal. This paper deals with the complexities of training personalized ASR models for Hindi by introducing a new methodology. Using only 14 minutes of personalized custom audio, a Retrieval-Based Voice Conversion (RVC) model is trained. This RVC model is the basis for creating a custom Common Voice 16 corpus made for Hindi. Then a Cross-lingual Self-supervised Representations (XLSR) Wav2Vec2 model is trained on this custom dataset, and it shows it can adapt even when resources are limited.

- GUI
  - user-friendly web GUI, built with Gradio
  - Hindi audio -> Hindi text (XLSR Wav2Vec2) -> English text (mBART)
  - input: video with Hindi audio; output: video with accurate English subtitles
- Contribution: ASR for low-resource languages; streamlined personalized transcription + translation pipeline for video

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Training an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model is a hard task, and how well the model works depends a lot on the quality of the dataset that is used in training. The challenge is even bigger when we try to train an ASR model for a low-resource language like Hindi, where there is much less data available online than for languages like English. It gets more complex again when the goal is to train a personalized ASR model for Hindi, one that does not just transcribe but also translates the unique voice of an individual. Generating a suitable dataset is a big hurdle for reaching this goal. This paper deals with the complexities of training personalized ASR models for Hindi by introducing a new methodology. Using only 14 minutes of personalized custom audio, a Retrieval-Based Voice Conversion (RVC) model is trained. This RVC model is the basis for creating a custom Common Voice 16 corpus made for Hindi. Then a Cross-lingual Self-supervised Representations (XLSR) Wav2Vec2 model is trained on this custom dataset, and it shows it can adapt even when resources are limited.

To make the trained model more useful in practice, a web-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) that is easy to use is also developed. The GUI is built with Gradio and it makes it simple to transcribe Hindi audio into Hindi text with XLSR Wav2Vec2 and then translate this Hindi text into English with mBART. The input to the system is a video that has Hindi audio, and the output is a video with accurate English subtitles. So this research contributes to the advancement of ASR technology for low-resource languages, and it offers a streamlined pipeline for personalized voice transcription and translation from Hindi audio to English (subtitle), made specifically for video content.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Training an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model is a formidable task, and the efficacy of the model is closely tied to the quality of the dataset used during training. The challenge becomes even more pronounced when training an ASR model for a low-resource language like Hindi, where the availability of online data is notably limited compared to languages such as English. The complexity grows further when the aim is to train a personalized ASR model for Hindi, one that not only transcribes but also translates an individual's unique voice. Generating an appropriate dataset is a significant hurdle in achieving this objective. This paper addresses the complexities of training personalized ASR models for Hindi by introducing an innovative methodology. Using just 14 minutes of personalized custom audio, a Retrieval-Based Voice Conversion (RVC) [1] model is trained. This RVC model serves as the basis for creating a tailored Common Voice 16 corpus specifically for Hindi. Subsequently, a Cross-lingual Self-supervised Representations (XLSR) Wav2Vec2 [2] model is trained on this custom dataset, showing adaptability even with limited resources. To increase the practical utility of the trained model, a user-friendly web-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) is developed. This GUI, powered by Gradio, simplifies transcribing Hindi audio to Hindi text using XLSR Wav2Vec2 and then translating this Hindi text to English using mBART [3]. The input to this system is a video containing Hindi audio, and the output is a video with accurate English subtitles. This research thus contributes to the advancement of ASR technology for low-resource languages, offering a streamlined pipeline for personalized voice transcription and translation from Hindi audio to English (subtitle), tailored specifically for video content.

References:
[1] , https://github.com/RVC-Project/Retrieval-based-Voice-Conversion-WebUI
[2] Arun Babu et al. “XLS-R: Self-supervised Cross-lingual Speech Representation Learning at Scale” In Proc. Interspeech 2022 , 2022, pp. 2278–2282 DOI: 10.21437/Interspeech.2022-143
[3] Yinhan Liu et al. “Multilingual Denoising Pre-training for Neural Machine Translation”, 2020 arXiv: 2001.08210 [cs.CL]
